_meta.source: CSS custom properties resolved from Airbnb's DLS stylesheets on airbnb.com (listing detail page), read via CSSOM + getComputedStyle, 2026-09-10
_meta.confidence: exact — these are the values the site ships, not estimates
_meta.use: Evidence for the constitution. We take the STRUCTURE (which scales exist, how many steps, how roles are named), never the values or the brand colours.

corner_radius_scale.note: eight named steps; observed use: 4 inputs/segments · 8 small buttons and text-button hover pads · 12 cards, medium buttons, sheets · 16 image tiles · 20 search-card image · 24 host identity card · 999 pill for the primary CTA and chips

spacing_scale.note: two ladders with different jobs: micro = inside a component, macro = between sections. They overlap at 16/24/32, which is where a component's outer padding meets a section's inner gap.

typography.family: 'Airbnb Cereal VF', 'Circular', -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Roboto, 'Helvetica Neue', sans-serif
structure_notes: Same size, two leadings: 14/18 (UI text) vs 14/20 (paragraph); 16/20 (UI) vs 16/22 and 16/24 (paragraph). The role encodes whether the text is scanned or read.
Titles come in two weights at the same sizes (medium 500, semibold 600) — emphasis is a weight step, never a size step.
Leading ratio ≈1.25–1.29 for UI text, 1.375–1.56 for reading text.
Display sizes exist (40–72) but do not appear on product surfaces; the largest product title is 26/30.
Observed on-page: 22px and 26px titles carry −2% tracking even though the token says 'normal' — applied at the component, not the token.
Every shadow starts with a 1px 2% ring — a hairline that survives on white — then adds blur. The hairline is the constant; the blur is the variable.
Numbered scale for authors; named aliases for roles. Same two-tier idea as ref/sys.

materials.note: five translucency steps for overlays over imagery (the Superhost pill uses a darker cousin: rgba(96,96,96,.6))

springs.note: mass 1 throughout; each spring is also shipped as a pre-sampled linear() easing so CSS can play it

primitive_ramps.beige: 100–1000 (#F7F6F2 … #232221) — a warm neutral ramp that exists alongside grey

structure_notes: Four text levels (primary/secondary/tertiary/quaternary) — same count as Apple's label hierarchy and as Enable's current sys-label set.
Four background levels plus 'interactive' and 'divider' as separate roles. A grey fill that can be pressed (#F2F2F2 interactive) is a different token from a grey fill that cannot (#F7F7F7 secondary).
Every interactive role has -hover, -pressed/-selected, -disabled siblings named, not derived. Disabled is a colour swap, not opacity.
State colours have a filled form (#D7251C) and a tint form (#FFE6E2) — ink on tint, never tint alone.
Brand chroma is confined to: logo, primary CTA gradient, search button, selected heart. The content layer is grey-scale plus status.
A warm 'beige' ramp exists as a parallel neutral (bg-surface-beige #F4F2EC, text-beige-primary #232221) — evidence that a warm neutral register coexists with the grey one inside the same system.
